introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: three and a quarter hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR QUESTIONS in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO questions from Section C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each. Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references. Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed. Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Using a pie chart with a **radius of 4 cm**, represent the population of the countries. *(12 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Principle.** A pie chart is a circle divided into sectors whose angles are proportional to the values. The whole circle (360 degrees) represents the total, 3,466 million.

**Step 1 - Check the total.** $1401 + 1282 + 325 + 255 + 203 = 3466$ million, which agrees with the printed total.

**Step 2 - Calculate the angles.** Angle $= \dfrac{\text{population}}{3466} \times 360^\circ$ (1 million is $360/3466 = 0.104^\circ$).

| Country | Population (million) | Share (%) | Angle (degrees) |
|---|---|---|---|
| China | 1,401 | 40.4 | 145.5, round to 146 |
| India | 1,282 | 37.0 | 133.2, round to 133 |
| USA | 325 | 9.4 | 33.8, round to 34 |
| Indonesia | 255 | 7.4 | 26.5, round to 26 |
| Brazil | 203 | 5.9 | 21.1, round to 21 |
| **Total** | **3,466** | **100** | **360** (146 + 133 + 34 + 26 + 21) |

**Step 3 - Construct.** With a compass draw a circle of radius 4 cm (diameter 8 cm) and mark the centre. Draw a vertical radius to 12 o'clock. With a protractor measure the angles clockwise from the radius, starting with the largest sector (China), then India, USA, Indonesia and Brazil. Check that the angles close the circle exactly.

**Step 4 - Finish.** Shade or colour each sector differently, label each sector with the country and its value (million or per cent), add a key and the title "Population of the five most populous countries, 2015" and the source.

![fig-1](gce-al-geography-2020-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_3_fig_1.png)

**Marking guide (12).** Calculations of angles 4 (correct method 2, accurate values 2); circle of radius 4 cm 1; accurate sectors with the protractor 3; shading and labels 2; title, key and source 2.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) What are the merits and demerits of using the technique in "a" above? *(2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Merits.** A pie chart is easy to draw and to read; it shows at once the share of each part in the whole, so the dominance of China and India (more than three-quarters of the total) is visible immediately; it is attractive and suits a non-specialist audience.

**Demerits.** It gives approximate values only (exact figures must be written on it); it is difficult to compare sectors that are close in size or to compare two different pie charts; it becomes crowded with many small sectors (here Indonesia and Brazil are small); the construction needs calculation and a protractor and takes time.

**Marking guide.** One well explained merit and one demerit earn 1 mark each (2 marks).

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Account for the large populations of China and India. *(3 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Both countries owe their very large populations to a long period of settlement, high natural increase and the ability to feed many people.
1. *Early and long settlement and favourable environments:* both have large fertile river plains (the Yangtze and Yellow River plains, the Indo-Gangetic plain) with alluvial soils and a monsoon climate, which allow intensive rice cultivation that can support very high densities; the long history of civilisation also meant a long period of population growth.
2. *High birth rates and falling death rates:* traditionally high fertility (early marriage, the preference for large families and for sons, little family planning) combined with falling death rates after the 20th century (better health care, vaccination, food security) produced rapid growth. Even where birth rates have fallen (China's one-child policy, later relaxed; India's family planning), *population momentum* keeps the numbers rising, because a large number of young adults are still having children.
3. *Large area and varied resources:* both are very large countries (millions of square kilometres), with varied resources that supported agriculture and later industry, which gave employment.

**Marking guide.** One mark for each reason clearly explained, up to 3.

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) State any **two** indicators of overpopulation? *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Overpopulation exists when there are too many people for the resources and technology of an area to support at an acceptable standard of living. Two indicators, each stated (1 mark) and explained (1 mark):
1. *Food shortage, hunger and malnutrition:* the food produced is not enough for the population, so there are frequent famines or the country depends on food imports and food aid.
2. *High unemployment and underemployment with low per capita income:* the number of job seekers is greater than the number of available jobs, wages are low and many people live in poverty, in the informal sector or in slums.

Other acceptable indicators: pressure on land (small and fragmented farms, land exhaustion, soil erosion and deforestation), shortage of housing and the growth of slums, overcrowded schools and hospitals, shortage of water and energy, high dependency ratio, high emigration, traffic congestion and pollution.

**Marking guide.** 2 marks for each indicator (statement 1, explanation or example 1).

questions.enonce_markdown: (e) Identify two measures that could be taken to redress the problems of over population. *(2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any two measures, each 1 mark:
1. *Family planning and education:* promote birth control, women's education and later marriage to reduce the birth rate, and use incentives and awareness campaigns.
2. *Increase the resources and jobs:* develop industry and services to create employment, raise food production by improved seeds, irrigation and fertilisers, and use better technology to raise the carrying capacity of the land.
3. *Redistribute the population:* resettlement schemes and rural development to reduce the pressure on crowded areas, and encourage migration to under-populated regions.

**Marking guide.** One mark for each measure correctly identified.
